clue.text: Capital city landlords

explanation.surface: Talk of the people who own property in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Capitals are upper-case print, and landlords letting out city blocks are jokingly people who let blocks.

clue.text: Mandatory work for a bookmaker

explanation.surface: Placing bets with a bookie is presented as a compulsory job.
explanation.definitionFit: A binding rule is compulsory; a bookbinder's craft of sewing and covering pages is also called binding.

clue.text: Unidentified person's broken nose

indicators.note: something broken is smashed into a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some anonymous victim has had their nose broken.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun for an unspecified individual takes the possessive form, as in minding your own business.

clue.text: Joint near which suggestive re marks are made

definitions.text: Joint near which suggestive re marks are made

parts.words: Joint near which suggestive re marks are made
parts.note: risque remarks are said to be near a particular finger joint, so the clue describes that joint by the idiom

explanation.surface: An innuendo is delivered close to some anatomical joint.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom near the knuckle means bordering on indecent, and the finger joint it names is the answer.

clue.text: Scattered shingle greeted their invasion of these shores

definitions.text: Scattered shingle greeted their invasion of these shores

indicators.note: pebbles scattered across a beach lie in a new order, so the letters of the beach word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pebbles on the beach met invaders landing on Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of SHINGLE is the whole clue's subject: the beach greeted the invading people whose name the country now bears.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anglo-Saxon invaders who landed on Britain's beaches became the nation named after the Angles.

clue.text: Order silence by an expression of scorn

annotationWithheld.why: Order silence by an expression of scorn (4): SH for silence is clear, but no clue word gives the TO; OCR text may be corrupt and no source found.
annotationWithheld.clue: Order silence by an expression of scorn

clue.text: Dessert which brings murmurs from the stage

definitions.text: which brings murmurs from the stage

explanation.surface: A pudding that makes actors mutter.
explanation.definitionFit: The pink stalks are stewed for puddings, and stage extras mutter the word to simulate crowd chatter.

clue.text: It is drawn with two vertical lines

definitions.text: It is drawn with two vertical lines

parts.words: It is drawn with two vertical lines
parts.note: drawn means written out against a bank account, and the two lines marked on it restrict payment to an account

explanation.surface: A sketch made with a pair of upright strokes.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank payment order marked with two parallel lines can only be paid into an account.

clue.text: Iron fire-grate modified for quite the opposite purpose

definitions.text: Iron fire-grate modified for quite the opposite purpose

indicators.note: an altered appliance is rebuilt, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An iron grate is converted to do the reverse of heating.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of IRON FIRE-GRATE gives a process that cools, the opposite of what a fire-grate does, so the whole clue defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping things cold is the reverse of a hearth's job of providing heat.

clue.text: Two-rhyme poem? No, a rude composition

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so these letters are assembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A critic rejects a form of verse as a crude piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: This French verse form of thirteen or so lines uses only two rhymes throughout.

clue.text: Guest troubled about body language

indicators.note: a troubled guest is stirred up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for concerning or about

explanation.surface: A visitor gets anxious over nonverbal signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A movement of the hands or head conveying meaning is a form of nonverbal communication.

clue.text: One between sun and earth

indicators.note: between means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Sol is the Latin name for the sun
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Something placed between the sun and our planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth in the gardener's sense is the ground plants grow in.

clue.text: Hank pushing point into hide

indicators.note: pushing one thing into another means it goes inside it

parts.note: an animal's hide is its skin
E is east, a compass point

explanation.surface: Someone named Hank sticks a sharp point into an animal pelt.
explanation.definitionFit: A hank is a coiled length of yarn or thread, as is a skein.

clue.text: Just a loud melody

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
an air is a tune

explanation.surface: Simply a noisy tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and even-handed are synonyms, as in a just decision.

clue.text: Dickensian gang-leader not out after a cigarette

indicators.note: after places the second piece behind the first

parts.note: fag is British slang for a cigarette
in cricket a batsman not out is still in

explanation.surface: A Victorian villain lights up while still batting.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batsman who is not out is still IN. FAG is everyday British slang for a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: The receiver of stolen goods in Oliver Twist runs a band of young pickpockets.

clue.text: Garden trailer that damages the plants

definitions.text: Garden trailer that damages the plants

parts.words: Garden trailer that damages the plants
parts.note: trailer suggests a cart but means a creature leaving a slimy trail as it eats plants

explanation.surface: A wheeled cart in the garden crushes the flowerbeds.
explanation.definitionFit: This slow mollusc leaves a slime trail and chews leaves, a familiar garden pest.

clue.text: Avenger disposed to scratch plate

indicators.note: disposed means arranged, so the letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A revenge-seeker is inclined to scrape the dinnerware.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting a design into a metal printing plate is the engraver's work.

clue.text: Army carrier giving worker the sack

parts.note: a hand is a manual labourer
a sack is a bag

explanation.surface: A military transport gives an employee the sack.
explanation.walkthrough: Army is read as arm-y: a carrier borne on the arm, not a military vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's bag for carrying belongings is typically hung from the arm.

clue.text: Pointedly ignoring news items worth keeping

explanation.surface: Snubbing newspaper stories that deserve saving.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone is to snub them; a press clipping is also called this.

clue.text: The most prickly of knightly orders

definitions.text: The most prickly of knightly orders

parts.words: The most prickly of knightly orders
parts.note: prickly is literal: Scotland's order of chivalry is named after a spiny plant

explanation.surface: One order of knights is the touchiest.
explanation.walkthrough: The Most Ancient and Most Noble Order of the Thistle is Scotland's highest order of chivalry; its spiny emblem is Scotland's national flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotland's chivalric order takes its name from the spiny weed that is Scotland's emblem.

clue.text: Excess weight is what he should fear

definitions.text: Excess weight is what he should fear

parts.note: a glut is an oversupply
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A man who ought to dread getting fat.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual overeater is the person most at risk of obesity.

clue.text: Cheerful potato slicer

explanation.surface: A happy gadget for cutting spuds.
explanation.definitionFit: Chipper is informal for lively; a machine cutting potatoes into fries does the job too.

clue.text: Browning reveals artist taken in by humpback

indicators.note: taken in by means the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: a camel has a hump on its back
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: The poet Browning shows an artist being swallowed by a whale.
explanation.definitionFit: Burnt sugar is used as a colouring agent, called gravy browning.

clue.text: East European flogging whip which is a real stinker

parts.note: a Pole comes from Poland in Eastern Europe
the cat-o'-nine-tails was a whip used for flogging

explanation.surface: A man from Poland whips someone who is a nasty piece of work.
explanation.definitionFit: This member of the weasel family gives off a foul smell when threatened.

clue.text: Live the wrong way and you will be so described

definitions.text: Live the wrong way and you will be so described

indicators.note: the wrong way means the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: A moral warning that leading a bad life earns a bad name.
explanation.walkthrough: Reversing LIVE gives the word, and living wickedly earns that very label, so the whole clue defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lives wickedly is called morally bad.

clue.text: Measure a quarter without hesitation

indicators.note: without means the second piece is dropped from the first

parts.note: a quarter is a fourth part
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Measure out a fourth part without dithering.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of liquid capacity equal to two pints.

clue.text: Nitwit left in bed

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A fool is abandoned lying in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Clot is British slang for a stupid person.

clue.text: Very old fashioned Egad!

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped anew, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the exclamation is the anagram fodder; the backwards run across the neighbouring word is a coincidence

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned oath exclaimed.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderly and advanced in years are synonyms.

clue.text: Former copper carpeted for ill egal junk

parts.note: D was the symbol for a pre-decimal penny, a copper coin
carpeted means covered by a rug, so the coin lies on a rug

explanation.surface: An ex-policeman is reprimanded for dealing in illicit goods.
explanation.walkthrough: Carpeted looks like reprimanded, and copper like policeman. D is the old British penny, a copper coin before decimal currency in 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: Junk is slang for narcotics, especially heroin.

clue.text: How to tie a dangerous captive when very nervous

definitions.text: How to tie a dangerous captive

explanation.surface: Advice on securing a prisoner, for someone tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Tied up firmly is how to bind a captive; a tense, anxious person is also described this way.

clue.text: Atlasarea of.W. Africa?

parts.note: the question invites a map page but means the country containing the Atlas Mountains

explanation.surface: Looking for a page of an atlas covering West Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The North-West African kingdom is where the Atlas Mountains run.

clue.text: Guide's torch for a leading activist

explanation.surface: A Girl Guide's flashlight belongs to the movement's foremost campaigner.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp that shows the way, or a prominent figure in a movement.
